output.title: What model deprecation hides in a small-business workflow
output.body:
Model deprecation sounds abstract until it reaches one recurring workflow. In practice, it can hide a simple cost: the thing that looked automated may need a rebuild when the model behind it changes or disappears.

That is the owner-level decision here. Before you treat AI as a replacement for manual work, ask whether the workflow is stable enough to tolerate change in the model layer, or whether it is safer to keep the task manual for now. The issue is not whether AI is useful. It is whether the business can live with the maintenance that sits underneath it.

Bareni’s diagnostic process starts with the recurring workflow itself. It identifies the task, says honestly whether AI fits, and then defines scope, price, and measures if a pilot makes sense. Timings are intended scopes, not guarantees. No tool removes model-deprecation risk entirely; at best, some choices can reduce how tightly one workflow depends on one model.

A practical next step is to pick one workflow and ask: if the model powering it were unavailable in 12 months, what would rebuilding that piece cost in time and attention compared with keeping it manual today? That question usually clears the fog. Human approval still stays in charge of the trade-off.
